items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: devotees of Artie Shaw or the Bob Crosby band

ctx.x: Problems in presenting it would you say?

Well I mean it has been buoyed up for a long time by people that are of the World War II generation who are now dying off. And people that heard — this whole generation that heard jazz at Eddie Condon’s and Nick’s in the Village and were also fans of the big bands and that were devotees of Artie Shaw or the Bob Crosby band or whatever. Those people are now all in their eighties if they’re still around. And so there’s not much opportunity – the music can’t be carried forward very much further on the strength of…

There was some talk this morning about labels and you really do have to label things sometimes. Like Mat Domber’s record label, he calls it classic jazz and we call some things traditional. And sometimes the word “trad” — I wonder if that word doesn’t have some connotations. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-
